# Lesson-planning worksheet

[← Documentation home](../README.md)

Copy this worksheet into your notes, complete it with your teaching team, then transfer the answers into Case Studio and Lesson Builder. Text in parentheses is guidance and can be deleted.

Do not place identifiable patient information in this worksheet.

---

## 3. Image preparation

**Image-readiness check:**

- [ ] Files are JPEG, PNG, or WebP—not raw DICOM.
- [ ] The order matches the intended visual reasoning sequence.
- [ ] The image source and rights have been checked.
- [ ] A person reviewed every visible pixel for identifiers.
- [ ] Burned-in labels, faces, and unique marks received special attention.
- [ ] The accessible description does not reveal the answer.

## 7. Objectives and evidence

Use one row per objective. Start with one to three. Add rows only when needed.

| Objective ID | Learner-facing objective | Assessment criterion | Observable evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | The learner will… | Satisfactory performance means… | The learner says or does… |
|  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |

**Objective quality check:**

- [ ] Each objective describes something a learner can do or say.
- [ ] Each criterion states the standard for satisfactory performance.
- [ ] Evidence can be observed in the conversation or learner action.
- [ ] The objectives fit this exact case and intended audience.
- [ ] The lesson can reasonably reach them without becoming a broad survey.

## 8. Tutor path

**Socratic opening:**
(The first focused question. Direct attention without naming the answer.)

### Hint ladder

Link every hint to an objective and move from least to most revealing.

| Hint ID | Linked objective ID | When it becomes useful | Hint text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hint-1` |  | Orient the learner |  |
| `hint-2` |  | Prompt a comparison |  |
| `hint-3` |  | Support interpretation |  |

### Escalation conditions

| Escalation ID | Observable condition | What the tutor may do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `escalation-1` | After… |  |
|  |  |  |

### Stopping conditions

| Stopping ID | Observable condition | Message to the learner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stopping-1` | When… |  |
|  |  |  |

(Tone, sequence, learner agency, and behavior to avoid.)

## 9. Sources

Artifact provenance identifies the image. Clinical teaching sources support medical or educational claims. A license page is not automatically either one.

| Source ID | Title | HTTPS URL or DOI | Role | Claim or artifact it supports | Verified by/date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source-1` |  |  | Artifact provenance / Clinical teaching |  |  |
| `source-2` |  |  | Artifact provenance / Clinical teaching |  |  |

**Source check:**

- [ ] Every URL or DOI opens and matches the title.
- [ ] The artifact-provenance source identifies the actual teaching image.
- [ ] Clinical claims have clinical-teaching support.
- [ ] A license deed is not being presented as clinical evidence.
- [ ] Sources found in an imported document were independently verified.

## 10. PDF or PowerPoint import, if used

**Source type:** PDF / PowerPoint / Not used

**Import purpose:**
(For example: start objectives from an existing faculty deck.)

**Import review:**

- [ ] Only one supported `.pdf` or `.pptx` was used.
- [ ] The preview matched the intended source.
- [ ] Duplicated headers, footers, and unrelated text were removed.
- [ ] Imported text was checked for identifiers.
- [ ] Topics were rewritten as observable objectives.
- [ ] Answer-revealing material was moved to educator-only notes.
- [ ] URLs and DOIs were verified rather than trusted automatically.
- [ ] The source document is not expected to appear in the export.
- [ ] No one expects pages or slides to become case images.

## 12. Learner rehearsal

Test the lesson with these responses:

| Rehearsal | What happened | Change needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correct observation, weak reasoning |  |  |
| Plausible incorrect answer |  |  |
| Request for a hint |  |  |
| Learner jumps to the diagnosis |  |  |
| Learner reaches the stopping condition |  |  |
| Lowest intended learner level |  |  |
| Highest intended learner level |  |  |

**Rehearsal check:**

- [ ] The opening directs attention without giving away the answer.
- [ ] The tutor asks for evidence.
- [ ] Hints are gradual and connected to objectives.
- [ ] Answer notes are not revealed too early.
- [ ] The stopping behavior is appropriate.
- [ ] The learner-facing text is accessible and understandable.

- [ ] A `.caseattend` backup was exported for a browser-created case.

- [ ] Recipients received the educational-use, privacy, rights, and review caveats.
- [ ] Release notes contain no identifiers.
